mostWorthwhile.text: Bringing river migration to a sheltered oasis was satisfying: it showed that moving to escape cold requires both a route and a suitable destination.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting cold-adapted populations and river migration only to find no available partners was initially confusing, especially when both seemed central to the goal.

surprise.text: Advancing ice could not initially be combined with the recovering world, but became usable with varied survivors. The later combination explained selection acting on inherited differences over generations.

arbitrary.text: Using the Sun to end the ice age felt compressed: warmth made intuitive sense, but the action did not explain the longer climate changes behind a retreat.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the recovered world unfolds; the contrasting routes through the ice age made its living history feel connected, while the explanations distinguished adaptation from individuals changing at will.
